newsitem.title: HUNGARY: BUDAPEST BOURSE CRITICISES EQUITY LAW DRAFT.
newsitem.headline: BUDAPEST BOURSE CRITICISES EQUITY LAW DRAFT.

text.p: The Budapest Stock Exchange (BSE) said on Thursday that a draft law on securities and supervision represents a step backwards in some respects and proposed changes to the legislation.

"There are a few details about which we think we ought to state our opinion so that the law should be better than its current draft," Zsigmond Jarai, chairman of the BSE's council, told a news conference.

Bourse council member Csaba Lantos, who is also director for fund management at Creditanstalt Securities, said the bourse's own governing status was one of the areas where the draft law needed to be revised.
"We would like to maintain the theoretical base on which the bourse operates...as it was in the previous law," said Lantos, referring to Hungary's 1990 statute.
The new draft law would give a bigger say to parties outside the bourse. Most bourse council members now came from bourse participants, but the draft would give them fewer seats on the council.
The current seven-member bourse council has two "external" members, representing the issuers and the investors.
Another area that came in for criticism was a section of the draft law dealing with competition, including inter-operability between the BSE and the Budapest Commodity Exchange (BCE).
Lantos said the BSE and the BCE already are cooperating.

Under one of the latest signs of their cooperation, the BSE and the BCE harmonised the date of introducing futures contracts for one- and three-month Budapest Interbank Offered Rates (BUBOR). Both started trading in BUBOR futures today.
The third area that came in for criticism was the draft law's provisions for protection of investors money.
"We agree to make the requirements stricter," Lantos said, but added these will results in higher costs.
The Hungarian government approved the draft legislation in late August and it is to be discussed by the Parliament.
